The as-built answer the reason waited on is now on file (docs/research/slipper_flank_robust/asbuilt.json, committed db95242 14:12; its note: 'is the crank-side cliff physical or a synthesis artefact?'). With the verified flank fixed and the crank built off-size, the drive keeps its stroke and stays on the flank: cases 'r_c -0.2 mm' stroke_at_stopB 49.65 (nominal 49.75), pa_crank_max 34.79 (< cap_kin 38.03), off_flank_rows 0, no_push_rows 0, K_rest 0; 'r_c -0.05/-0.1 mm' PA 31.47/32.74, stroke 49.72/49.70; asbuilt_extra.log r_c -0.3/-0.4/-0.5/-1.0 mm: PA 36.28/37.91/39.0/43.59, stroke 49.6/49.55/49.51/49.36, off 0, nopush 0; 'g -0.02 (lobe)' stroke 50.17, PA 29.5; 'beta -1 deg' stroke 48.77, PA 23.6. So 'the stroke goes to 0' (fit 14.25 -> 86.1) belongs to RE-SYNTHESISING the drive per neighbour (the synthesis refuses PA > cap and returns dK 0), not to the built part: the built crank reaches the 38.03 kinematic cap only at r_c about -0.45 mm, about 90x the +-5 um bore tolerance the red team specifies (slipper_mechanism_redteam.md finding 8), and keeps its 49.4-49.7 deg stroke beyond it. Together with the score steps the audit already read (beta steps 18.43-18.48), the pattern costs the wearer nothing as built. The fold-margin exposure the same table shows is a T3 matter (ruled there).
